title: Tio's father and uncle; Papa Tio's dislike of jazz
summary: He remembers the older Tio, his softer tone, and the old man's disdain for jazz.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: Yeah, it's hard to say. I think about Baby Dodds and Johnny Dodds. I guess you didn't know the Dodds brothers, do you remember them? I don't remember them. I knew of them after they left. I knew them both in Chicago. Johnny never took a drink in his life hardly and Baby was quite a drinker. Yeah. Johnny died when he was 48 and Baby kept drinking and drinking and the other he lived to be 65 or so. That's right. Doesn't usually really kill him, but it might make it a little worse if they have that stroke. Maybe he had that trouble too, but he kept on. Johnny died from sort of a stroke then, weren't you? Johnny died of a stroke. Oh, speaking of the T.O.'s, do you remember the older men, either the old Lorenzo or the Papa? I remember the uncle for Papa very well. I don't remember Lorenzo's daddy. Lorenzo Senior, but I do remember. I think he was, I think it was the old man. Is it Louie T.O.? Louie T.O. That's his name. The brother that's still living. Yeah. Said that their father went back, I believe, to over on the Gulf Coast, either Biloxi or something. Bay St. Louis. That's where they were. You remember the uncle then? Oh, I remember the uncle very well. How did he compare with, in playing with the young Lorenzo? Well, if you can remember well enough to the sound, I know it's... The sound, I think the sound was about the same. And

the old man was more of a, like we would use the term, was more of a softer player than Lorenzo. Lorenzo was more forceful. But the sound was almost the same. I don't think it just wasn't that much in
volume, you see? And you remember in your childhood, the youngest, very youngest, remembrance is that the old man was still teaching that his papa was... Yeah, I can remember because

he died in 22. He died in 22. I can remember very well when he died. He used to visit home quite often. He and his wife both. He was a friend of your father. Yeah, he was. Because the father was most old as a son or something under him, you see. And he's... And at one time, they were neighbors too. And Mrs. Teal and the old man, they used to visit home often. And I can remember them on the street, but like I said before, I used to remember the playing and the style. I can't... I really can't remember his playing.

I remember once, speaking of Natty Dominic again, he said he remembers when he was a little boy, once Papa Teal heard a jazz band like out on a wagon or something and came running in their house and wanted to hide under the bed or something. That noise is a disgrace to music. It's a disgrace to New Orleans. He didn't really like jazz. He liked classical music. He did. Yeah, I guess so. I think even symphonic work he did his time and conducted that group and everything else.
